translations.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen sojourners scattered throughout Pontus and Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia,

according to the foreknowledge of God the Father and through the holiness of the Spirit, for obedience and for the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ. Grace be with you, and may peace be multiplied!
Blessed is God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who in his great mercy has begotten us anew to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
to an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled and unfading, kept in the heavens for you,
you who are guarded by the power of God through faith for the salvation that is ready to be revealed in the last time.
In this you now rejoice, though for a little while, if it must be, you have been grieved by many kinds of trials,
so that the testing of your faith, more precious than perishable gold that is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ,
whom you did not know, yet you love him; whom you do not see now, yet you believe in him. Rejoice with a joy that is unspeakable and glorious,
and may you receive, at the end of your faith, the salvation of souls.
Concerning this salvation the prophets searched and inquired, those who prophesied to you about the grace that was to come,
searching when, or at what time, the Spirit of Christ among them was making it known, when he testified beforehand to them about the sufferings of Christ and the glories that would follow.

It was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but you in the things that have now been announced to you by your evangelists through the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, things that the angels long to look into.
Therefore gird up the loins of your minds, be watchful, and set your hope fully on that grace of theirs [?] that is coming at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
As children of obedience, do not be conformed to the former desires of your ignorance,
but just as the one who called you is holy, you also be holy in all your conduct.
For it is written: "Be holy, for I am holy."
And if you call on him as Father, who judges each person's deeds without partiality, live out the time of your sojourning in fear.
Know that you were redeemed from the futile way of life handed down by your fathers, not with perishable silver or gold,
but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish and without spot,
who was foreknown before the creation of the world but was revealed in these last times for your sake;
through him you have come to believe in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God.
Purify your souls by obedience to the truth through the Spirit; for the sake of brotherly love be without hypocrisy, and love one another earnestly from a pure heart.
You have been born a second time, not of perishable seed but of imperishable, through the word of the living God, which abides forever.
For all flesh is grass, and all human glory is like the flower of grass: the grass withered and its flower fell away.
But the word of God endures forever, and this is the word that was proclaimed to you as good news.
So put away all wickedness and all deceit and hypocrisy and envy and every kind of evil speech.
Like newborn children, long for that pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow.
if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is good,
Come to him, the living stone, which was rejected by men but is chosen and precious in God's sight.
And you also, like living stones, are being built up into a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
For it is written in Scripture: "Behold, I am laying in Zion a cornerstone, chosen and precious, and whoever believes in him will never be put to shame."
So to you who believe there is honour; but for the disobedient, "the stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner," and "a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence."
They stumble at the word through disobedience, and to this they were also appointed.
But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy seed, a people acquired as his own, so that you may proclaim the virtues of him who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.
Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
Beloved, I urge you, as strangers and sojourners, to keep away from the desires of the flesh, which wage war against the soul.
Keep your conduct among the Gentiles good, so that in the matter in which they speak evil of you as evildoers, they may be put to shame by your good works and glorify God on the day of visitation.
Therefore submit to every human institution for the Lord's sake: whether to the king, since he is over all,
or to governors, as sent by him to punish those who do evil and to praise those who do good.
For this is the will of God: that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish people.
Live as free people, and do not use your freedom as a cover for wickedness, but live as servants of God.
Honour everyone, love the brothers, fear God, honour the king.
Servants, submit to your own masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the harsh.
For this is grace from God: when someone, out of a good conscience toward God, endures afflictions, even if he suffers unjustly.
For what is better about it if you sin and are punished and endure it? But if you do good and suffer and endure it, this is grace from God.
For to this very thing you were called, because Christ also suffered for us and left you a written pattern, so that you might follow in his footsteps.
He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth.
When he suffered, he reviled no one; when he suffered, he spoke against no one [threatened no one]; the righteous one handed himself over to the judge.
He bore our sins in his own body on the cross, so that we might be separated from sin and live by righteousness. By his wounds you were healed.
For you were like sheep that had gone astray, but now you have turned to the Shepherd and Guardian of your souls.
Likewise, wives, be submissive to your own husbands, so that even if some of them disobey the word, they may be won over without a word by the conduct of their wives,
when they see your holy conduct in fear,
and let your adornment not be the outward braiding of hair and the putting on of gold, or the wearing of fine clothing,
but the hidden person of the heart, with the incorruptible manner of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious before God.
For this is how the holy women of old, who hoped in God, used to adorn themselves, and they were submissive to their own husbands,
as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord. You have become her children if you do good and are not afraid, not even of any terror.
Husbands, likewise, live with them with consideration, giving honour to the women as to the weaker vessel, as fellow heirs of the grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered.
Finally, all of you be of one mind, merciful, loving the brethren, kind, humble.
Do not repay evil for evil, or abuse for abuse, but bless the one who opposes you, and know that you were called for this very purpose, that you may inherit a blessing.
For whoever wishes to love life and to see good days, let him keep his tongue from evil and let his lips not speak deceit;
let him turn away from evil and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it.
For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous and his ears are open to their prayer, but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.
And who is there who will do you harm if you become imitators of what is good?
And even if you suffer for righteousness' sake, you are blessed. Do not fear what they fear, and do not be troubled.
But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you for an account of the hope that is in you, with gentleness and fear.
Keep a good conscience, so that those who speak evil of you as of evildoers, those who treat your good conduct in Christ with violence, may be put to shame.
For it is better, if the will of God should so ordain your suffering, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil.
For Christ also suffered once for our sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, so that he might bring us to God. He was put to death in the flesh and made alive in the spirit,
in which he also went to the prison of the spirits and preached
to those who were once disobedient, when the long-suffering of God waited once in the days of Noah, while the ark was being prepared, in which a few, that is, eight souls, were saved from the water.
In the likeness of this, baptism now saves you too: not the removal of filth from the flesh, but the longing of a good conscience toward God, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
who is at the right hand of God, who ascended into heaven, and angels, authorities and powers were made subject to him.
Since Christ suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves also with the same mind, for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin,
so that you may live the remaining time in the flesh no longer by human desires but by the will of God.
For the time of this life that has already passed is enough for us to have done the will of the gentiles, who walk in impure desires, drunkenness, revelling, carousing and lawless idolatry.
They are surprised that you do not run with them into the same confusion of impurity, and they revile you.
They will give an account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
For this is why the gospel was preached to the dead: so that they might be judged in the flesh as humans are, and live through God in the spirit.
The end of all things is near. So be pure, and be watchful in prayer.
Above all, keep your love for one another fervent, for love covers a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
Each of you should use the gift you have received to serve one another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.

Whoever speaks should speak as one speaking the words of God. Whoever serves should serve as one serving by the strength that God supplies, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ. To him belong glory and might for ever and ever. Amen.
Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal among you that is happening to you as a trial, as though something strange were happening to you.
Rather, rejoice insofar as you share in the sufferings of Christ, so that you may also rejoice and be glad when his glory is revealed.
If you are reproached for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you. As they see it, you are reviled, but as you see it, you are glorified.
Let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evildoer, or as a meddler in other people's affairs.
But if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in this lot.
For the time has come for judgment to begin, and it begins first with the house of God. And if it begins first with us, what will the end be for those who disobey the gospel of God?
And if the righteous person is barely saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?
So from now on, those who suffer according to the will of God should entrust their souls to the faithful Creator by doing good.

I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and as one who shares in the glory that is to be revealed hereafter: shepherd the flock of God that is among you,
taking care of it not under compulsion but willingly, as God wants, and not for shameful gain but eagerly.
Do not lord it over those entrusted to you, but be an example to the flock.
And when the chief shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.
Likewise, you who are young, submit to the elders. And all of you, in submission to one another, clothe yourselves with humility, for God crushes the proud but gives grace to the humble.
Humble yourselves, therefore, under the mighty hand of God, so that he may exalt you in his own time.
Cast all your care on him, for he cares for you.
Be watchful and stay awake, for your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour.
Resist him, firm in faith, knowing that you are undergoing the same sufferings as your brotherhood in this world.
And the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory through Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little, will himself strengthen you, establish you, empower you and make you firm.
To him be glory and might for ever and ever. Amen.
Through Silvanus, your faithful brother, as I regard him, I have written to you briefly, exhorting you and testifying that this is the true grace of God, in which you stand.
The one who is in Babylon, together with the chosen one, greets you, and so does Mark, my son.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace be with you, all of you who are through Christ Jesus. Amen.
